40	attribute [local instance] AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.functionFieldOverModule
41	  AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.overModule
42	
43	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
44	
45	open Scheme
46	
47	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
48	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
49	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
50	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
51	
52	/-! ## The pointwise minimum -/
53	
54	/-- The candidate multiplicities of the base divisor of `T` relative to `A` at the closed
55	point `p`: the values `(A + div f)ₚ` over nonzero `f ∈ T`, truncated to `ℕ` (faithful once
56	`T ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A))`, which makes every `A + div f` effective). -/
57	def Scheme.baseDivisorSet (T : Submodule K X.functionField) (A : X.CurveDivisor)
58	    (p : {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X}) : Set ℕ :=
59	  {n : ℕ | ∃ (f : X.functionField) (_ : f ∈ T) (hf : f ≠ 0),
60	    (coeffAt p.2
61	      (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))).toNat = n}
62	
63	/-- **The base multiplicity of `T` relative to `A` at a closed point**: the minimum of
64	`(A + div f)ₚ` over nonzero `f ∈ T`. -/
65	noncomputable def Scheme.baseDivisorAt (T : Submodule K X.functionField)
66	    (A : X.CurveDivisor) (p : {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X}) : ℕ :=
67	  sInf (Scheme.baseDivisorSet K T A p)
68	
69	lemma Scheme.baseDivisorSet_nonempty {T : Submodule K X.functionField}
70	    (A : X.CurveDivisor) (hT : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0) (p : {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X}) :
71	    (Scheme.baseDivisorSet K T A p).Nonempty := by
72	  obtain ⟨f, hfT, hf⟩ := hT
73	  exact ⟨_, f, hfT, hf, rfl⟩
74	
75	/-! ## The assembled base divisor -/
76	
77	/-- **The base divisor `bd(T)` of a subspace `T` relative to `A`**: the Weil divisor of
78	pointwise base multiplicities. Finitely supported because `0 ≤ bd(T)ₚ ≤ (A + div f₀)ₚ`
79	for the chosen nonzero `f₀ ∈ T`. -/
80	noncomputable def Scheme.baseDivisor (T : Submodule K X.functionField)
81	    (A : X.CurveDivisor) (hT : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0) : X.CurveDivisor :=
82	  Finsupp.onFinset
83	    (toFinsupp (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
84	      (Units.mk0 hT.choose hT.choose_spec.2))).support
85	    (fun p => (Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T A p : ℤ))
86	    (fun p hp => by
87	      rw [Finsupp.mem_support_iff]
88	      intro hzero
89	      apply hp
90	      have hle : Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T A p
91	          ≤ (coeffAt p.2 (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
92	              (Units.mk0 hT.choose hT.choose_spec.2))).toNat :=
93	        Nat.sInf_le ⟨hT.choose, hT.choose_spec.1, hT.choose_spec.2, rfl⟩
94	      have hc : coeffAt p.2 (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
95	          (Units.mk0 hT.choose hT.choose_spec.2)) = 0 := hzero
96	      omega)
97	
98	/-- The pointwise value of the base divisor is the base multiplicity. -/
99	lemma Scheme.coeffAt_baseDivisor {T : Submodule K X.functionField} {A : X.CurveDivisor}
100	    (hT : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0) {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
101	    coeffAt hx (Scheme.baseDivisor K T A hT)
102	      = (Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T A ⟨x, hx⟩ : ℤ) :=
103	  rfl
104	
105	/-- **The base divisor is effective.** -/
106	lemma Scheme.baseDivisor_nonneg {T : Submodule K X.functionField} {A : X.CurveDivisor}
107	    (hT : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0) : 0 ≤ Scheme.baseDivisor K T A hT := by
108	  refine CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr (fun x hx => ?_)
109	  rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, Scheme.coeffAt_baseDivisor K hT hx]
110	  positivity
111	
112	/-! ## The lower-bound and achiever properties -/
113	
114	/-- Under `T ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A))`, the shifted divisor `A + div f` of a nonzero `f ∈ T` is
115	effective at every closed point. -/
116	lemma Scheme.coeffAt_add_divOf_nonneg {T : Submodule K X.functionField}
117	    {A : X.CurveDivisor} (hTA : T ≤ divisorSections K A ⊤) {f : X.functionField}
118	    (hfT : f ∈ T) (hf : f ≠ 0) {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
119	    0 ≤ coeffAt hx
120	      (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf)) := by
121	  have hmem := hTA hfT
122	  rw [mem_divisorSections_top_iff K hf] at hmem
123	  have h := CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mp hmem x hx
124	  rwa [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero] at h
125	
126	/-- **The lower-bound property of the base divisor**: `bd(T) ≤ A + div f` pointwise, for
127	every nonzero `f ∈ T`. -/
128	lemma Scheme.baseDivisorAt_le_coeffAt {T : Submodule K X.functionField}
129	    {A : X.CurveDivisor} (hTA : T ≤ divisorSections K A ⊤) {f : X.functionField}
130	    (hfT : f ∈ T) (hf : f ≠ 0) {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
131	    (Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T A ⟨x, hx⟩ : ℤ)
132	      ≤ coeffAt hx
133	          (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf)) := by
134	  have h1 : Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T A ⟨x, hx⟩
135	      ≤ (coeffAt hx
136	          (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))).toNat :=
137	    Nat.sInf_le ⟨f, hfT, hf, rfl⟩
138	  have h2 := Scheme.coeffAt_add_divOf_nonneg K hTA hfT hf hx
139	  omega
140	
141	/-- **The achiever**: at every closed point, some nonzero `f ∈ T` attains the base
142	multiplicity: `(A + div f)ₓ = bd(T)ₓ`. -/
143	lemma Scheme.exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt {T : Submodule K X.functionField}
144	    {A : X.CurveDivisor} (hTA : T ≤ divisorSections K A ⊤) (hT : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0)
145	    {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
146	    ∃ (f : X.functionField) (_ : f ∈ T) (hf : f ≠ 0),
147	      coeffAt hx (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))
148	        = (Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T A ⟨x, hx⟩ : ℤ) := by
149	  have hmem : Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T A ⟨x, hx⟩ ∈ Scheme.baseDivisorSet K T A ⟨x, hx⟩ :=
150	    Nat.sInf_mem (Scheme.baseDivisorSet_nonempty K A hT ⟨x, hx⟩)
151	  obtain ⟨f, hfT, hf, heq⟩ := hmem
152	  refine ⟨f, hfT, hf, ?_⟩
153	  have h2 := Scheme.coeffAt_add_divOf_nonneg K hTA hfT hf hx
154	  omega
155	
156	/-! ## The normalization: `T ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A − bd T))` with no residual base point -/
157	
158	/-- **The base-divisor normalization**: `T ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A − bd T))` — every nonzero `f ∈ T`
159	has `(A − bd T) + div f ≥ 0` because `bd(T)` is a pointwise minimum. -/

203	/-- **An effective witness of a class of large degree.** If a Weil divisor `W` has
204	`1 ≤ deg W + χ(𝒪)` then its Čech Picard class is realized by an **effective** divisor. The
205	Riemann inequality (`riemann_inequality`) forces a nonzero global section `f` of `𝒪(W)`, i.e.
206	`f ∈ K(X)ˣ` with `W + div f ≥ 0`; that shift is effective and of the same class
207	(`CurveDivisor.picClass_divOf`). -/
208	lemma exists_effective_of_picClass (W : X.CurveDivisor)
209	    (hW : 1 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W + Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K)) :
210	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = CurveDivisor.picClass K W := by
211	  -- `h⁰(𝒪(W)) ≥ 1`, so `H⁰` is nontrivial.
212	  have hfr : 0 < Module.finrank K (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K W) 0) := by
213	    have h1 : (1 : ℤ) ≤ (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K W) : ℤ) :=
214	      le_trans hW (riemann_inequality K W)
215	    have : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K W) := by omega
216	    exact this
217	  haveI : Nontrivial (Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K W) 0) :=
218	    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos hfr
219	  -- a nonzero global section `g ∈ 𝒪(W)(⊤) ⊆ K(X)`.
220	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := exists_ne (0 : Sheaf.HModule (X.divisorSheaf K W) 0)
221	  set s := (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀ (Opens.grothendieckTopology (X : TopCat))
222	    (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) (X.divisorSheaf K W)) t with hs
223	  have hsne : s ≠ 0 := by
224	    rw [hs]; exact (LinearEquiv.map_ne_zero_iff _).mpr ht
225	  set g : X.functionField := divisorVal K s with hg
226	  have hgmem : g ∈ divisorSections K W ⊤ := divisorVal_mem K s
227	  have hgne : g ≠ 0 := by
228	    intro h
229	    exact hsne (divisorSection_ext K
230	      (show divisorVal K s = divisorVal K (0 : _) from by rw [← hg, h]; rfl))
231	  -- the unit `u` and the effective shift.
232	  set u : X.functionFieldˣ := Units.mk0 g hgne with hu
233	  have huval : (u : X.functionField) = g := rfl
234	  refine ⟨W + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) u, ?_, ?_⟩
235	  · -- effectivity: `coeffAt (W + div u) ≥ 0` from the pole bound
236	    refine Finsupp.le_def.mpr (fun p => ?_)
237	    change (0 : ℤ) ≤ coeffAt p.2 (W + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) u)
238	    have htop : ((⊤ : X.Opens) : Set X).Nonempty := ⟨genericPoint X, trivial⟩
239	    have hb := (mem_divisorSections_of_nonempty K htop).mp hgmem p.1 p.2 trivial
240	    rw [← huval, Scheme.ord_val_eq K u p.2, divisorBound_le_iff p.2,
241	      CurveDivisor.coeffAt_neg] at hb
242	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add]
243	    omega
244	  · -- same class
245	    rw [CurveDivisor.picClass_add, CurveDivisor.picClass_divOf, mul_one]

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorClassMeromorphic
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.MulEquiv
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.SectionSpaces
9	
10	/-!
11	# DAT-C C3 — effective uniqueness at `h⁰ = 1`
12	(`informal/w4-datc-worksheet.md` GAP-2, Σ-UNIQ-fld)
13	
14	The field-level uniqueness brick of the canonical-section normalization: on the curve
15	bundle `X` over a field `K`, an effective divisor `D` with `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1` is the
16	**unique** effective representative of its Čech Picard class.
17	
18	Route (worksheet §0.3 GAP-2, verbatim): equal classes give a rational function `g`
19	with `div g = D' − D` (`CurveDivisor.exists_divOf_of_picClass_eq`); `g ∈ H⁰(𝒪(D))`
20	since `div g + D = D' ≥ 0` (`mem_divisorSections_top_iff`); `1 ∈ H⁰(𝒪(D))` since
21	`0 ≤ D`; `h⁰ = 1` forces `g = c · 1` (`finrank_eq_one_iff_of_nonzero'` through the
22	`h⁰` bridge `finrank_divisorSections_top`), and a nonzero constant has trivial
23	principal divisor, so `D' − D = div g = 0`.
24	
25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ord_functionFieldOverAlgebraMap_eq_one` — a nonzero
26	  constant has trivial order valuation at every closed point.
27	* `Scheme.divOf_eq_zero_of_val_eq_functionFieldOverAlgebraMap` — a unit of `K(X)`
28	  whose value is a constant has trivial principal divisor.
29	* `Scheme.one_mem_divisorSections_top` — `1 ∈ H⁰(𝒪(D))` for effective `D`.
30	* `Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_finrank_one` — the worker, with the
31	  section-space hypothesis `dim_K H⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1`.
32	* `Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` — **the keystone**: `0 ≤ D`,
33	  `0 ≤ D'`, equal classes, `h⁰(𝒪(D)) = 1` imply `D' = D`.
34	-/
35	
36	set_option autoImplicit false
37	
38	universe u
39	
40	open CategoryTheory Opposite
41	
42	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
43	
44	attribute [local instance] Scheme.functionFieldOverModule Scheme.overModule
45	
46	namespace Scheme
47	
48	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
49	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
50	
51	/-! ## Constants have trivial order and trivial principal divisor -/
52	
53	/-- **A nonzero constant has trivial order valuation at every closed point**: both `c`
54	and `c⁻¹` are integral (`ord ≤ 1`), and their orders multiply to `ord 1 = 1`. -/

8	/-!
9	# DD-0 — the section bound `h⁰(𝒪(A)) ≤ max 0 (deg A + 1)`
10	
11	The section-bound half of the DAT-D brick DD-0 (`informal/dat-d-worksheet.md` §5 DD-0,
12	consumed by the P-fib normalization step F1 of §3.3): on the curve bundle `X` (integral,
13	smooth of relative dimension one, quasi-compact over a field `K`, with finite `H⁰`/`H¹`
14	of `𝒪_X`), the global-section count of any divisor sheaf is bounded by its degree,
15	
16	`h⁰(𝒪(A)) ≤ max 0 (deg A + h⁰(𝒪_X))`,
17	
18	hence `≤ max 0 (deg A + 1)` when `h⁰(𝒪_X) = 1` (the geometrically-integral curve value,
19	`ChiCurve.h0_moduleKSheaf`; kept as an explicit hypothesis here so the ledger layer stays
20	on the abstract bundle).
21	
22	## Route (worksheet §5 DD-0: "peeling on the landed slice SES; base case via
23	effective-witness degree ≥ 0")
24	
25	* **`h¹` never drops under effective twists** (`h1_add_single_le` →
26	  `h1_add_effective_le`): the dévissage SES `0 → 𝒪(D − x) → 𝒪(D) → sky → 0` has
27	  skyscraper cokernel with no `H¹`, so the slice machinery
28	  (`Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f`, `ChiSlice.lean`) gives a surjection
29	  `H¹(𝒪(D − x)) ↠ H¹(𝒪(D))`; peel point by point exactly as `peel_effective`
30	  (`FLVClass.lean`). In particular `h¹(𝒪(E)) ≤ h¹(𝒪_X)` for `E ≥ 0`
31	  (`h1_le_of_effective`).
32	* **The effective witness** (`exists_effective_of_h0_pos`): a nonzero global section of
33	  `𝒪(A)` is a rational function `g` with `A + div g ≥ 0`, an *effective* divisor of the
34	  same class — the extraction of `exists_effective_of_picClass` run from `0 < h⁰`
35	  directly (no Riemann inequality needed). This is the base case: `0 < h⁰ ⟹ deg A ≥ 0`.
36	* **Assembly** (`h0_le_deg_add_h0_of_pos`, keystone `h0_divisorSheaf_le_max`): if
37	  `h⁰(𝒪(A)) > 0`, replace `A` by the effective witness `E` (class-invariance of `h⁰` and
38	  `deg`, `ClassCohomology`/`Degree`), then the χ-ledger `chi_divisorSheaf` reads
39	  `h⁰(𝒪(E)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg E + h¹(𝒪(E)) ≤ deg A + h⁰(𝒪_X)`.
40	
41	The `h¹`-monotonicity lemmas are exported (not private): F1's window comparisons reuse
42	them, and they are the natural `H¹`-side companion of `peel_effective`.
43	-/

57	    (hlam : degAt lam (Over.testPoint t) = 0)
58	    (ht : t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam) :
59	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L)
60	        (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L)
61	        (_ : Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L)
62	        (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L)
63	        (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
64	        (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
65	      PicEtAff.map C L
66	          (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t)
67	            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)))
68	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) ∧
69	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M ∧
70	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) ∧
71	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
72	        ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1) ∧
73	      (Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) : ℤ)
74	        = (n : ℤ) + 1 - (g : ℤ) := by
75	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM, W, hWcl, hWh1⟩ := ht
76	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
77	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
78	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
79	  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
80	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
81	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
82	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
83	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
84	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
85	  have hWdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) := by
86	    rw [← classDeg_picClass (K := L) W, hWcl,
87	      classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff C L _ M hM]
88	    change degAt (chartTwist C m Z T lam) (Over.testPoint t) = (n : ℤ)
89	    rw [chartTwist, degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_mul, degAt_thetaFamily_pow,
90	      degAt_sigmaFamily, hlam, hdeg]
91	    ring
92	  have hχL : Sheaf.chi (((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (g : ℤ) :=
93	    chi_relCurve_baseField C L g hχ
94	  have hrank := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := L) W hWh1
95	  rw [hWdeg, hχL] at hrank
96	  refine ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, W, hM, hWcl, hWdeg, hWh1, ?_⟩
97	  omega
98	
99	/-- Above the genus parameter, chart-locus membership supplies a witness with at least two
100	sections.  Thus the
101	large-parameter vanishing route and the `h⁰ = 1` uniqueness route are genuinely different
102	branches of the representability argument. -/
103	theorem exists_splitting_two_le_h0_of_mem_chartLocus
104	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
105	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (n g : ℕ)
106	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
107	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
108	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
109	    (hlam : degAt lam (Over.testPoint t) = 0) (hgn : g < n)
110	    (ht : t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam) :
111	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L)
112	        (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L)
113	        (_ : Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L)
114	        (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L)
115	        (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
116	        (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
117	      PicEtAff.map C L
118	          (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t)
119	            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)))
120	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) ∧
121	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M ∧
122	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) ∧
123	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
124	        ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1) ∧
125	      2 ≤ Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) := by
126	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, W, hM, hWcl, hWdeg, hWh1,
127	      hrank⟩ := exists_splitting_h0_formula_of_mem_chartLocus
128	        lam t m Z n g hdeg hχ hlam ht
129	  refine ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, W, hM, hWcl, hWdeg, hWh1, ?_⟩
130	  have htwo : (2 : ℤ) ≤
131	      (Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) : ℤ) := by
132	    rw [hrank]
133	    omega
134	  exact_mod_cast htwo
135	
136	/-! ## The actual unconditional coverage parameter -/
137	
138	/-- On a positive-genus curve, the unconditional admissible coverage parameter is strictly
139	larger than the genus.
140	
141	The strictness does not add a cohomological hypothesis: `h⁰(𝒪_C) = 1` follows from the standing
142	proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible assumptions.  If the ledger contribution above `g`
143	were nonpositive, `genus_eq_zero_of_windowBound_nonpos` would contradict `g ≠ 0`. -/
144	theorem genus_lt_admissibleCoverageParameter_of_ne_zero
145	    {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
146	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
147	    (g : ℕ) (hg : g ≠ 0)
148	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ)) :
149	    letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
150	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
151	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
152	    haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
153	    haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
154	      inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
155	    haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
156	      inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
157	    haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
158	      moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
159	    haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
160	      moduleFinite_hModule_one C
161	    g < admissibleCoverageParameter (C := C) hπ g := by
162	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
163	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
164	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
165	  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
166	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
167	    inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
168	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
169	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
170	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
171	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
172	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
173	    moduleFinite_hModule_one C
174	  have hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 := h0_moduleKSheaf C
175	  have hb : 0 < windowBound π hπ := by
176	    by_contra hnonpos
177	    exact hg (genus_eq_zero_of_windowBound_nonpos π hπ g
178	      (not_lt.mp hnonpos) hO hχ)
179	  have hM := windowBound_le_M_mul π hπ g
180	  have hledger : (g : ℤ) <
181	      (windowM_choice π hπ g : ℤ) * windowδ π + (g : ℤ) := by
182	    omega
183	  have hadmissible := ledgerBound_le_admissibleCoverageParameter (C := C) hπ g
184	  have hcast : (g : ℤ) <
185	      (admissibleCoverageParameter (C := C) hπ g : ℤ) :=
186	    hledger.trans_le hadmissible
187	  exact_mod_cast hcast
188	
189	/-- For positive genus, the uniform full-locus coverage chart supplies a splitting witness with
190	at least two sections at every degree-zero fibre point.
191	
192	This is the direct join between `exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart` and the rank formula:
193	the large parameter solves vanishing and coverage, but it cannot simultaneously be read as the
194	genus-parameter `h⁰ = 1` chart used by the unique-effective-representative route. -/
195	theorem exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_two_le_h0
196	    {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] [IsDominant π]
197	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
198	    (g : ℕ) (hg : g ≠ 0)
199	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ)) :
200	    letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
201	    haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
202	      inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
203	    haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
204	    haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
205	      inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
206	    haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
207	      inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
208	    haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
209	      moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
210	    haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
211	      moduleFinite_hModule_one C
212	    ∃ (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor),
213	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
214	          = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)
215	            - (admissibleCoverageParameter (C := C) hπ g : ℤ) ∧
216	        ∀ {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left),
217	          degAt lam (Over.testPoint t) = 0 →
218	            ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
219	                (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L)
220	                (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L)
221	                (_ : Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L)
222	                (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L)
223	                (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
224	                (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
225	              PicEtAff.map C L
226	                  (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t)
227	                    (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)))
228	                = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) ∧
229	              Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M ∧
230	              Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W
231	                = (admissibleCoverageParameter (C := C) hπ g : ℤ) ∧
232	              Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
233	                ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1) ∧
234	              2 ≤ Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) := by
235	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := ⟨C.hom⟩
236	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
237	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
238	  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
239	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
240	    inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
241	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
242	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
243	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
244	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
245	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
246	    moduleFinite_hModule_one C
247	  obtain ⟨m, Z, hZ, hcover⟩ := exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart hπ g hχ
248	  refine ⟨m, Z, hZ, ?_⟩
249	  intro T lam t hlam
250	  exact exists_splitting_two_le_h0_of_mem_chartLocus lam t m Z
251	    (admissibleCoverageParameter (C := C) hπ g) g hZ hχ hlam
252	    (genus_lt_admissibleCoverageParameter_of_ne_zero hπ g hg hχ)
253	    (hcover lam t hlam)
254	
255	end
256	
257	end AlgebraicGeometry

1	/-

5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.EffectiveUniqueness
8	
9	/-!
10	# The chart locus SUPPLIES GAP-2's binders rather than needing them
11	
12	Seven files cite the keystone by name (measured, case-insensitively, at HEAD: `Pic0ChartLocus`,
13	`Pic0ChartUnivReduce`, `Pic0ChartPair`, `Pic0ChartAbelNonInjective`, `Pic0ChartAbelForkReduce`,
14	`JacobianDataAbelDegreeWindow`, and `RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness` itself); the chart-layer
15	ones name the *relative form of DAT-C GAP-2* as the residue of
16	`ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor` (`Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:140`; that file is
17	**outside this one's import closure**, so the name is unresolvable here and is cited by
18	location rather than bare — `I-1173`), and price its field-level keystone
19	`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one` (`RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean:144`)
20	as landed-but-unfed: what a lane still owes, they say, are that keystone's three binders
21	`hD`, `hD'` (effectivity) and `hone` (`h⁰ = 1`).
22	
23	**On the chart locus all three are consequences.**  The reason is visible in the definition
24	and was apparently never read off it: `chartLocus` is *defined* by the very vanishing the rank
25	anchor consumes.  `IsSplitWitness` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:151`) asserts, at a point, the
26	existence of a finite separable `L/κ(t)`, a presenting Čech class `M`, and a `CurveDivisor W`
27	in that class with `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))`.  So membership already carries a divisor with
28	`h¹ = 0`; what it does not carry is that divisor's *degree*, and the degree comes from
29	outside, from the chart-index constraint.
30	
31	## The chain, every link landed before this file
32	
33	1. `classDeg_presenting_eq_degAff` (`Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean:85`) reads the
34	   `L`-degree of the presenting class as the plus-degree of the class it presents;
35	2. the twist ledger (`chartTwist` unfolded through `degAt_mul`/`degAt_inv`/
36	   `degAt_thetaFamily_pow`/`degAt_sigmaFamily`) turns that into `m·d₁ − deg_k Z`, which the
37	   chart-index constraint `hdeg` makes exactly `n`;
38	3. `chi_relCurve_baseField` transports `χ(𝒪) = 1 − n` to the base-changed curve;
39	4. the rank anchor `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`
40	   (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) gives `h⁰ = deg + χ = n + (1 − n) = 1`;
41	5. `exists_effective_of_h0_pos` (`RiemannRoch/SectionBound.lean:175`) then produces an
42	   **effective** divisor of the same class, so effectivity is free too;
43	6. `h0_divisorSheaf_eq_of_picClass_eq` (`RiemannRoch/ClassCohomology.lean:89`) carries the
44	   `h⁰` value across to it.
45	
46	## What this is NOT
47	
48	* It is **not** `hb_forces_h0_eq_one` (`Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean:180`).  That takes a
49	  *threshold* hypothesis — every divisor of degree `≥ n` has `H¹ = 0` — which its own file
50	  proves **false** at `n = g` (a moving degree-`g` family has `h⁰ ≥ 2`).  Nothing here assumes
51	  a threshold: the vanishing is supplied by the locus at **one** divisor, the one the
52	  membership witness names.  A statement about one divisor of degree `n` is not a statement
53	  about all of them, and only the former is true.
54	* It does **not** discharge `exists_factor`, and therefore closes no antecedent of
55	  `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`.  Everything here is **fibrewise**: it lives over a splitting
56	  field `L/κ(t)` at a single point `t`.  Per the standing caveat of
57	  `Pic0ChartAbelNonInjective.lean`, uniqueness of the *fibre* witness is not injectivity of
58	  the chart at a general test — the gap measured as `RelPicSeparatesDivFamZar`
59	  (`Pic0ChartAbelForkReduce.lean:237`, also outside this file's closure).  What is removed is
60	  one *named input* of the field-level keystone, not the relativisation.
61	* `n = genus C` is **not** proved here and is not assumed either: `n` is whatever the chart
62	  index is legal at, and `hχ : χ(𝒪_C) = 1 − n` is a hypothesis.  Per `I-1176`,
63	  `chi_moduleKSheaf` *converts* that pinning rather than supplying it, so the binder stays
64	  explicit and its supplier stays named.
65	
66	## Main declarations
67	
68	* `h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_of_deg` — the rank anchor at a witness of the pinned degree.
69	* `exists_splitting_h0_eq_one_of_mem_chartLocus` — **the converse of
70	  `mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1`**: from locus membership, a witness with `h⁰ = 1`.
71	* `eq_of_picClass_eq_of_deg_of_subsingleton` — the keystone with `hone` discharged.
72	* `exists_effective_picClass_eq_of_h0_eq_one` — effectivity is free once `h⁰ = 1`.
73	* `existsUnique_effective_of_mem_chartLocus` — **the payoff**: at a locus point the class has
74	  an effective representative that is the unique one, with all three keystone binders supplied.
75	-/
76	
77	set_option autoImplicit false
78	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
79	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
80	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
81	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
82	
83	universe u
84	
85	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
86	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
87	
88	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
89	
90	open AlgebraicJacobian
91	
92	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
93	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
94	
95	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
96	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
97	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
98	
99	noncomputable section
100	
101	/-- **The rank anchor at a witness of the pinned degree.** -/
102	theorem h0_eq_one_of_subsingleton_of_deg
103	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
104	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
105	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
106	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
107	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
108	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
109	    (n : ℕ) (hχ : Sheaf.chi (((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
110	    (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
111	    (hW : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ))
112	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)) :
113	    Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) = 1 := by
114	  have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := L) W h1
115	  rw [hW, hχ] at hanchor
116	  omega
117	
118	/-- **THE CONVERSE OF `mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1`, WITH THE `h⁰` VALUE READ OFF.** -/
119	theorem exists_splitting_h0_eq_one_of_mem_chartLocus
120	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : T.left)
121	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ)
122	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
123	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
124	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
125	    (hlam : degAt lam (Over.testPoint t) = 0)
126	    (ht : t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam) :
127	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L)
128	        (_ : IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L)
129	        (_ : Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L)
130	        (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L)
131	        (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
132	        (W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor),
133	      -- `M` presents the TWISTED fibre class at `t`: this is what ties the conclusion to
134	      -- `lam`, `m`, `Z` and `t`, and without it the statement is satisfied by `W = 0`.
135	      PicEtAff.map C L
136	          (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t)
137	            (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) (chartTwist C m Z T lam)))
138	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M) ∧
139	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M ∧
140	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W = (n : ℤ) ∧
141	      Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) = 1 := by
142	  obtain ⟨L, hLf, hLa, hLKa, hLtow, hLfin, hLsep, M, hM, W, hWcl, hWh1⟩ := ht
143	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
144	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
145	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
146	  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
147	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
148	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
149	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
150	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=

/-- **The converse direction: every nonnegative threshold is realised.**

Given a threshold `b ≥ 0` and a legal chart index at parameter `b.toNat`, the `hdeg` of
`mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` holds **by construction**.  So `hdeg` is not an
unsatisfiable hypothesis and coverage-at-a-chart-index is not blocked by it — which is the half
of the reviewer's report that needs correcting.

What this does *not* do is put the index at the representability parameter `n = g`.  That is the
whole remaining question, and `hb_forces_h0_eq_one` says what it would cost to answer it by
taking `b = g`. -/
theorem index_of_threshold {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T) (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T)
    (hlam : degAt lam t = 0)
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
    (M₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.CechPic)
    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K (picEtMap C t lam))
      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) (b : ℤ) (hb0 : 0 ≤ b)
    (hZ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - b) :
    classDeg L (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map
        ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap (Algebra.ofId k L)).left) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
      = ((b.toNat : ℕ) : ℤ) := by
  rw [classDeg_presenting_twist C lam t hlam L M₀ hM₀ m Z, hZ, Int.toNat_of_nonneg hb0]
  ring

/-! ## What the threshold hypothesis costs at `b = n` -/

/-- **`hb` at `b = n` is the SHARP vanishing, and the χ-ledger turns it into an `h⁰` equality.**

If every divisor of degree `≥ n` on the base-changed curve has `H¹ = 0`, then on a curve with
`χ(𝒪) = 1 − n` **every** divisor of degree exactly `n` has `h⁰ = 1`.

This is the sharpened form of the reviewer's strength observation.  Their version — "strictly
stronger than any threshold result" — is a comparison with what the tree has; this is a
comparison with what is *true*: for `n = g ≥ 1` a degree-`g` divisor may well have `h⁰ ≥ 2` (any
`g`-tuple of points imposing dependent conditions), so `hb` at `b = g` is not merely unproved,
it is **false in general**.  Hence there is no route to B-5 that instantiates DAT-0a at `b = g`,
and the residue is the chart-parameter reconciliation described in the module docstring.

One line from the rank anchor `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`
(`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) — recorded because the whole argument fits in it and the
conclusion is worth having in Lean rather than in a review comment. -/
theorem hb_forces_h0_eq_one
    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
    (n : ℕ) (hχ : Sheaf.chi (((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (n : ℤ))
    (hb : ∀ D : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
      (n : ℤ) ≤ Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D →
        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L D) 1))
    (D : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
    (hD : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D = (n : ℤ)) :
    (Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L D) : ℤ) = 1 := by
  have h1 := hb D (le_of_eq hD.symm)
  have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := L) D h1
  rw [hD, hχ] at hanchor
  omega

end

122	Stated with the witness clause on a *presenting Čech class* rather than on a datum,
123	because the datum layer is where the shifted-datum constructor (DAT-C GAP-1) is missing;
124	the two agree through `Pic0ChartLocusClass.mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.
125	
126	## A convention this predicate INHERITS, and which a consumer must not misread
127	
128	The worksheets say "effective degree-`g` witness with `h¹ = 0`".  The witness clause here —
129	and the tree's `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.HasWitnessH1Vanishing`
130	(`Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:115`) that it mirrors, and the GAP-6 dictionary
131	`subsingleton_h1_tensor_iff_exists_witness` (`DivisorFamilyH1Locus.lean:182`) that both rest
132	on — asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  It asks only for a `CurveDivisor` in the
133	class with vanishing `H¹`.  That is deliberate on the tree's side: the dictionary is an *iff*
134	against the engine's complex-form condition `Subsingleton (H¹(pair D) ⊗ L)`, and that
135	condition cannot see effectivity or degree, so adding either clause would break the iff and
136	with it the openness route.
137	
138	Two consequences, both load-bearing:
139	
140	* the degree is supplied **externally**, by the chart-index constraint through
141	  `degAt_chartTwist` below: on a degree-zero `λ` the twisted class has fibre degree
142	  `m·d₁ − deg Z`, which the constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − g` makes `+g`.  It is *not* a
143	  hypothesis of this predicate.  (Until 2026-07-28 this read `−g`, and that sign made the
144	  locus empty for every `g ≥ 1` — see `degAt_chartTwist` and issue I-0514;
145	  `chartTwist_chartValue` now pins the direction by the kernel);
146	* effectivity likewise is not asserted here.  Where the *worksheet's* stronger reading is
147	  actually needed — the canonical-section normalization `h⁰ = 1`, and GAP-2 uniqueness
148	  (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`, which does take `0 ≤ D`, `0 ≤ D'`) — the
149	  effectivity must be re-supplied at that point.  A lane that reads `IsSplitWitness` as
150	  already giving it will have a gap where it least expects one. -/
151	def IsSplitWitness {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
152	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) : Prop :=
153	  ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
154	      (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)
155	      (M : (relCurve C L).CechPic),
156	    PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
157	        = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M)
158	      ∧ ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
159	          Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W = M
160	            ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
161	                ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W) 1)
162	
163	/-! ## The twisted fibre family -/
164	
165	variable (C) in
166	/-- **The twisted family whose chart-membership `chartLocus` tests**: the plus class `λ`
167	shifted by the Σ-family of `Z` and by `m` inverse powers of the pinned θ-family.
168	
169	This is the *class-side* half of `chartValue` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`): where
170	`chartValue` twists the Abel class of a divisor family, `chartTwist` twists an arbitrary
171	plus class by the same two factors.  A point of `chartLocus` is precisely a point at which
172	`chartTwist` is realised by an effective divisor with no `H¹` — i.e. at which `λ` itself is
173	a chart value, after undoing the twist. -/
174	def chartTwist (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
175	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) : picEt C T :=
176	  lam * (thetaFamily C (thetaCechClass C) T ^ m) * (sigmaFamily C Z T)⁻¹
177	
178	/-- **The degree ledger of the twist**: at every field point the twisted family has fibre
179	degree `m·d₁ − deg Z` when `λ` is degree-zero.  With the chart-index constraint
180	`deg Z = m·d₁ − g` this is `+g`, which is the degree at which an effective witness with
181	`h¹ = 0` can exist at all.
182	
183	**Sign discipline, and it was wrong here until 2026-07-28 (issue I-0514).**  `chartTwist`
184	must be the INVERSE of `chartValue`'s twist, not the same one.  `chartValue` is
185	`abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` (`DivSchemeAbel.lean:351`), so recovering the Abel class from a chart
186	value means multiplying by `θᵐ` and dividing by `Σ` — hence `chartTwist` is
187	`λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`.  An earlier version applied the `chartValue` twist itself, giving fibre degree
188	`deg Z − m·d₁ = −g`; since `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))` forces `deg W ≥ g − 1`, that locus was
189	**empty for every `g ≥ 1`** and its openness was the openness of `∅`.  The comparison point is
190	`degAt_chartValue` at `n = g` (where the chart index is calibrated and `chartValue` lands in
191	`pic0`), NOT at `n = 0`.
192	
193	**An independent confirmation that `+g` is the right target**, worth recording because the
194	wrong sign survived two sessions: at `deg W = g` the rank anchor
195	`h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one` (`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean:412`) gives, for a
196	witness with `h¹ = 0`,
197	`h⁰ = deg W + χ(𝒪) = g + (1 − g) = 1` — exactly the `h⁰ = 1` normalization that DAT-C §2 and
198	GAP-2's uniqueness both require.  So `+g` is not merely the sign that makes the locus nonempty;
199	it is the unique degree at which the witness is *unique*, which is what the chart map needs to be

7	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.DivisorSheafZero

9	/-!
10	# The field-dictionary endgame: the DivEq converse, forward injectivity, the equiv reduction
11	(`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 (f), the DD-1c inverse-law adjudication)
12	
13	The forward map `divFamDivisor` (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyField`) sends a
14	certified divisor family over the field `K` to its Weil divisor, and is `DivEq`-invariant
15	(`Scheme.presentationDivisor_eq_of_divEq`). This file lands the **converse** and the
16	**injectivity** it powers, and packages the **equiv reduction** — the exact assembly of the
17	frozen `divFamFieldEquiv` from the two remaining, precisely-named gaps.
18	
19	* `Scheme.divEq_of_presentationDivisor_eq` — the **converse of DivEq-invariance**: two
20	  local-equation systems on the curve with the *same* Weil divisor are divisor-equal. On the
21	  common refinement of the two covers the ratio of the anchor equations is a unit at every
22	  closed point (equal orders read the equal divisor coefficient off any piece,
23	  `MeromorphicPresentation.ordZ_elem_eq` + `coeffAt_presentationDivisor`), hence — being an
24	  `𝒪(0)`-section together with its inverse (`exists_section_germ_eq`) — a genuine unit
25	  section that rescales one system to the other. Together with the landed
26	  `presentationDivisor_eq_of_divEq` this is the characterization
27	  `DivEq d₁ d₂ ↔ presentationDivisor d₁ = presentationDivisor d₂`.
28	
29	* `divFamDivisor_injective` — the **forward map is injective**: two families with equal
30	  divisor are `DivEq`, hence equal in the setoid `DivFam`. This is *unconditional* (no
31	  Mayer–Vietoris, no backward construction); it is the injective half of `divFamFieldEquiv`,
32	  and it *is* the second inverse law `divFamOfDivisor (divFamDivisor F) = F` once the
33	  backward map exists (both sides then present the same divisor).
34	
35	* `divFamFieldEquivOfDegOfSurj` — the **equiv reduction**: given the two remaining gaps —
36	  `hdeg` (the general colength↔degree identity `deg (divFamDivisor F) = n` for an *arbitrary*
37	  certified family, the honest Mayer–Vietoris wall) and `hsurj` (backward realization: every
38	  effective degree-`n` divisor is the divisor of some certified family, discharged over `K`
39	  by the support-separated construction whose certificate rank is `deg = n` *for free* via
40	  `deg_divFamDivisor_of_separated`, no general MV) — the equiv
41	  `DivFam C K π n ≃ {D // 0 ≤ D ∧ deg K D = n}` drops out (injectivity is already free).
42	
43	## Adjudication verdict (for the DD-R spec that consumes this dictionary)
44	
45	The full `divFamFieldEquiv` needs **exactly two** further inputs, and neither is the second
46	inverse law (that is landed here as `divFamDivisor_injective`):
47	
48	1. `hdeg` — LANDED (2026-07-18, I-0230): `deg_divFamDivisor` in
49	   `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyFieldCRT` proves the forward degree
50	   unconditionally; the glued colength is adaptation-independent
51	   (`DivisorAdaptation.deg_presentationDivisor`), dissolving the I-0179 MV wall this
52	   paragraph used to describe.
53	2. `hsurj` — the backward realization (a support-separated certified family per effective
54	   degree-`n` divisor, via `PointPresentation.pointEquations` products). Large but **does
55	   not** need general MV: its certificate's `finrank W = deg D = n` is the *separated*
56	   identity applied to the constructed adaptation with `deg D = n` an input hypothesis.
57	
58	**One-sidedness for DD-R.** If P-fib supplies a *unique* effective degree-`n` divisor `D`,
59	then `hsurj`'s family for `D` feeds the dictionary and the one landed law
60	`divFamDivisor (family) = D` round-trips through the divisor; and because `divFamDivisor` is
61	mono (`divFamDivisor_injective`) — so its section is determined — the second inverse law is
62	not separately required. DD-R can therefore consume the one-sided dictionary (backward map +
63	`divFamDivisor_injective`) and need **not** fund the general-MV brick, provided ε (DD-4) is
64	mono so family equality can be tested after ε.
65	-/

69	universe u
70	
71	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
72	
73	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
74	
75	namespace Scheme
76	
77	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
78	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
79	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
80	
81	/-- **The converse of DivEq-invariance** (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 (f), the second
82	inverse-law core): two local-equation systems on the curve `X` with the *same* Weil divisor
83	are divisor-equal. On the common refinement `d₁.cover ⊓ d₂.cover`, at each point `x`, the
84	ratio `r = elem₁ x / elem₂ x` of the anchor equations has order `1` at every closed point of
85	the overlap — the equal divisor coefficient read off either piece
86	(`MeromorphicPresentation.ordZ_elem_eq`, `coeffAt_presentationDivisor`) — so both `r` and
87	`r⁻¹` are `𝒪(0)`-sections (`exists_section_germ_eq`), i.e. `r` is a unit section rescaling
88	`d₂.eqn x` to `d₁.eqn x`. The converse of `Scheme.presentationDivisor_eq_of_divEq`. -/
89	theorem divEq_of_presentationDivisor_eq {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations}
90	    (h : presentationDivisor K d₁.presentation = presentationDivisor K d₂.presentation) :
91	    LocalEquations.DivEq d₁ d₂ := by
92	  refine ⟨d₁.cover ⊓ d₂.cover, inf_le_left, inf_le_right, fun x => ?_⟩
93	  have hηW : genericPoint X ∈ d₁.cover.opens x ⊓ d₂.cover.opens x :=
94	    ⟨d₁.cover.genericPoint_mem_opens x, d₂.cover.genericPoint_mem_opens x⟩
95	  have hWne : ((d₁.cover.opens x ⊓ d₂.cover.opens x : X.Opens) : Set X).Nonempty :=
96	    ⟨genericPoint X, hηW⟩
97	  simp only [PointedCover.inf_opens]
98	  set r : X.functionFieldˣ :=
99	    d₁.presentation.elem x * (d₂.presentation.elem x)⁻¹ with hr
100	  -- `r` is a stalk-unit at every closed point of the overlap
101	  have hru : ∀ (z : X) (hz : z ≠ genericPoint X),
102	      z ∈ d₁.cover.opens x ⊓ d₂.cover.opens x →
103	      Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz r = 1 := by
104	    intro z hz hzW
105	    have e1 := d₁.presentation.ordZ_elem_eq K hz (y := x) hzW.1
106	    have e2 := d₂.presentation.ordZ_elem_eq K hz (y := x) hzW.2
107	    have hcoeff := congrArg (coeffAt hz) h
108	    rw [coeffAt_presentationDivisor, coeffAt_presentationDivisor] at hcoeff
109	    have hzz : Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz (d₁.presentation.elem z)
110	        = Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz (d₂.presentation.elem z) :=
111	      Multiplicative.toAdd.injective hcoeff
112	    have hkey : Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz (d₁.presentation.elem x)
113	        = Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz (d₂.presentation.elem x) :=
114	      e1.trans (hzz.trans e2.symm)
115	    rw [hr, map_mul, map_inv, hkey, mul_inv_cancel]
116	  -- both `r` and `r⁻¹` are `𝒪(0)`-sections over the overlap
117	  have hmem : ∀ (g : X.functionFieldˣ),
118	      (∀ (z : X) (hz : z ≠ genericPoint X), z ∈ d₁.cover.opens x ⊓ d₂.cover.opens x →
119	        Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz g = 1) →
120	      (g : X.functionField) ∈ divisorSections K 0 (d₁.cover.opens x ⊓ d₂.cover.opens x) := by
121	    intro g hg
122	    rw [mem_divisorSections_of_nonempty K hWne]
123	    intro z hz hzW
124	    rw [divisorBound_zero]
125	    exact le_of_eq
126	      ((Scheme.ordZ_eq_one_iff (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz g).mp (hg z hz hzW))
127	  have hrinv : ∀ (z : X) (hz : z ≠ genericPoint X),
128	      z ∈ d₁.cover.opens x ⊓ d₂.cover.opens x →
129	      Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz r⁻¹ = 1 := by
130	    intro z hz hzW
131	    rw [map_inv, hru z hz hzW, inv_one]
132	  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := exists_section_germ_eq K hηW (hmem r hru)
133	  obtain ⟨s', hs'⟩ := exists_section_germ_eq K hηW (hmem r⁻¹ hrinv)
134	  -- `s` and `s'` are inverse sections, giving the rescaling unit
135	  have hss' : s * s' = 1 :=
136	    germ_injective_of_isIntegral X (genericPoint X) hηW (by
137	      rw [map_mul, hs, hs', map_one, ← Units.val_mul, mul_inv_cancel, Units.val_one])
138	  have hs's : s' * s = 1 := by rw [mul_comm]; exact hss'
139	  have hu : (↑(⟨s, s', hss', hs's⟩ : Γ(X, d₁.cover.opens x ⊓ d₂.cover.opens x)ˣ) :
140	      Γ(X, d₁.cover.opens x ⊓ d₂.cover.opens x)) = s := rfl
141	  refine ⟨⟨s, s', hss', hs's⟩, ?_⟩
142	  -- the rescaling equation, verified at `η` by germ injectivity
143	  refine germ_injective_of_isIntegral X (genericPoint X) hηW ?_
144	  have hL : (X.presheaf.germ (d₁.cover.opens x ⊓ d₂.cover.opens x) (genericPoint X) hηW).hom
145	        ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (d₁.eqn x))
146	      = (d₁.presentation.elem x : X.functionField) := by
147	    rw [X.presheaf.germ_res_apply]; exact (d₁.presentation_elem_val x).symm
148	  have hR : (X.presheaf.germ (d₁.cover.opens x ⊓ d₂.cover.opens x) (genericPoint X) hηW).hom
149	        ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d₂.eqn x))
150	      = (d₂.presentation.elem x : X.functionField) := by
151	    rw [X.presheaf.germ_res_apply]; exact (d₂.presentation_elem_val x).symm
152	  rw [map_mul, hu, hs, hL, hR, hr, Units.val_mul, Units.val_inv_eq_inv_val, mul_assoc,
153	    inv_mul_cancel₀ (d₂.presentation.elem x).ne_zero, mul_one]
154	
155	end Scheme
156	
157	/-! ## Forward injectivity and the equiv reduction on `DivFam` over a field -/
158	
159	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
160	
161	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
162	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
163	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
164	variable [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)]
165	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
166	  [QuasiCompact (relCurve C K ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
167	variable {n : ℕ}
168	
169	/-- **The forward map `divFamDivisor` is injective** (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 (f)): two
170	divisor families over the field `K` with the same Weil divisor are `DivEq`
171	(`Scheme.divEq_of_presentationDivisor_eq`), hence equal in the setoid `DivFam`.
172	
173	This is *unconditional* — no Mayer–Vietoris degree identity, no backward construction — and
174	it is the injective half of the field dictionary `divFamFieldEquiv`. It is also the second
175	inverse law `divFamOfDivisor (divFamDivisor F) = F` once the backward map exists: both sides
176	present the same divisor `divFamDivisor F`, so injectivity forces them equal. -/
177	theorem divFamDivisor_injective :
178	    Function.Injective (divFamDivisor : DivFam C K π n → (relCurve C K).CurveDivisor) := by
179	  refine fun F G => Quotient.inductionOn₂ F G (fun F' G' hFG => ?_)
180	  exact Quotient.sound (Scheme.divEq_of_presentationDivisor_eq K
181	    (d₁ := F'.eqns) (d₂ := G'.eqns) hFG)
182	
183	/-- **The field dictionary, assembled from the two remaining named gaps**
184	(`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 (f), the frozen `divFamFieldEquiv`). Given
185	
186	* `hdeg` — the **general** colength↔degree identity `deg (divFamDivisor F) = n` for an
187	  *arbitrary* certified family (the honest Mayer–Vietoris wall of I-0179; needed even to land
188	  the forward map in the degree-`n` subtype), and
189	* `hsurj` — **backward realization**: every effective degree-`n` divisor is the divisor of
190	  some family (discharged over `K` by the `PointPresentation.pointEquations`-product
191	  support-separated construction, whose certificate rank is `deg D = n` *for free* via
192	  `deg_divFamDivisor_of_separated` — this direction needs no general MV),
193	
194	the field dictionary `DivFam C K π n ≃ {D // 0 ≤ D ∧ deg K D = n}` drops out: injectivity is
195	already free (`divFamDivisor_injective`), effectivity is landed (`zero_le_divFamDivisor`).
196	
197	The two hypotheses are exactly the DD-1c residue: `hsurj` is a fundable construction, `hdeg`
198	is the sole general-MV obligation. See the module docstring for the DD-R consumption note. -/
199	noncomputable def divFamFieldEquivOfDegOfSurj
200	    (hdeg : ∀ F : DivFam C K π n,
201	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K (divFamDivisor F) = (n : ℤ))
202	    (hsurj : ∀ D : (relCurve C K).CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ D →
203	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K D = (n : ℤ) → ∃ F : DivFam C K π n, divFamDivisor F = D) :
204	    DivFam C K π n
205	      ≃ {D : (relCurve C K).CurveDivisor // 0 ≤ D ∧ Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K D = (n : ℤ)} :=
206	  Equiv.ofBijective
207	    (fun F => ⟨divFamDivisor F, zero_le_divFamDivisor F, hdeg F⟩)
208	    ⟨fun F G hFG => divFamDivisor_injective (Subtype.ext_iff.mp hFG),
209	     fun D => by
210	       obtain ⟨F, hF⟩ := hsurj D.1 D.2.1 D.2.2
211	       exact ⟨F, Subtype.ext hF⟩⟩
212	
213	end AlgebraicGeometry

104	theorem isCertified_of_deg {n : ℕ}
105	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg K
106	      (Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation) = (n : ℤ)) :
107	    A.IsCertified n := by
108	  haveI hfin : ∀ j, Module.Finite K (A.colength j) := A.moduleFinite_colength
109	  haveI : Module.Finite K A.chartProd := Module.Finite.pi

113	    have hZ := A.deg_presentationDivisor
114	    rw [hdeg] at hZ

116	  refine

/-!
# Sections to divisors — the DAT-A2 germ-regularity bridge

The geometry layer of the `lm:ctn` (iii)⟹(i) slicing criterion
(`informal/spec-dat-a.md` §2; core: `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FibrewiseRegular`):

* **(α) germ transport** — `IsAffineOpen.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors`: a nonzerodivisor of
  the section ring of an affine open has nonzerodivisor germs at all of its points
  (stalks are localizations of the affine section ring; regularity passes to
  localizations). This is also the "germ-level regularity by localization-exactness"
  consumption surface of DD-1a (dat-d-worksheet §1.2).
* **(the field-level slice case, Kleiman tex 2013–2022)** —
  `Scheme.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero`: on an **integral** scheme a nonzero
  section has nonzerodivisor germs everywhere on its open. This is the named lemma
  DAT-C discharges at field-level fibres ("nonzero on the integral fibre ⟹ regular").
* **(β) piece flatness** — `flat_sections_basicOpen`: over `Spec k`, if the affine
  chart ring is `k`-flat (`Scheme.overModule`) then so is every basic-open piece ring
  (tower `k → Γ(V) → Γ(D(h))` through `IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen`).
* **(γ) the generic A2 bridge** — `mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_fibrewise_regular` (+ germ
  form): over a Noetherian `k`, a section of a basic-open piece of a `k`-flat affine
  chart that is **fibrewise regular** (multiplication injective on every residue-field
  fibre of the piece ring, in `Scheme.mulSectionEnd`/`rTensor` form) is a nonzerodivisor
  with nonzerodivisor germs. The tensor-RING form of the fibre hypothesis converts
  through `injective_rTensor_mulSectionEnd_of_tmul_mem_nonZeroDivisors`.
* **(δ) A2 on the pinned datum** — for `D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` and a global
  section `s` of the DAT-1 glued sheaf, each component `D.component s j` (the section on
  the trivializing basic-open piece `D(h_j)`) is a nonzerodivisor with nonzerodivisor
  germs, given its fibrewise regularity (`component_mem_nonZeroDivisors`,
  `germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors`). These are exactly the `regular` inputs of
  `Scheme.LocalEquations` — the LocalEquations construction and the class law are in
  `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionsToDivisorsClass`.

The fibrewise hypothesis is deliberately the *piece-ring residue-fibre* spelling
(worksheet §2.2.2 with §5 risk 4 discharged): it is vacuous on pieces missing a fibre
(zero ring), it is exactly what the integral-fibre slice case produces where the fibre
ring is a domain, and it keeps the un-landed 1d-ii/DAT-3 fibre-sheaf identifications
with their owners (DAT-C/DD-R bridge their fibre-curve statements to this spelling).
-/

8	/-!
9	# THE FORK'S TARGET IS AN EQUALITY OF `relPic` CLASSES, PIECEWISE — the twist cancels and
10	the plus unit is injective
11	
12	`Picard/Pic0ChartAbelNonInjective.lean` reduces the non-injectivity fork to divisor families:
13	a witness owes two *distinct* elements of `divFamZar C π n T` whose `chartValue` agree.  Its
14	closing paragraph, and three other sites, then price what remains on the *positive* side of
15	the fork — `ChartFibrePresented.exists_factor` — as "the relative form of DAT-C GAP-2", and
16	state that **nothing in the tree** concludes `s₁ = s₂` for two `divFamZar` sections from an
17	equality of their classes.
18	
19	This file measures what that equality of `chartValue`s actually *is*, and the answer is two
20	steps shorter than the fork's own file suggests.
21	
22	## The two steps, and why neither is bookkeeping
23	
24	1. **The twist cancels.**  `chartValue s = abelDiv s · Σ_Z · (θ^m)⁻¹` in the abelian group
25	   `picEt C T`, and the two twist factors do not depend on `s`.  So `chartValue s₁ =
26	   chartValue s₂` is *equivalent* to `abelDiv s₁ = abelDiv s₂` — an `Iff`, by
27	   `mul_left_inj`/`mul_right_cancel`, with `m`, `Z` and `hdeg` playing no role at all.
28	   This matters because every statement of the fork carries `m`, `Z` and `hdeg`, and they are
29	   decoration in it: a witness-builder owes nothing about the twist, and a `Z` of the wrong
30	   degree cannot rescue injectivity.
31	2. **The plus unit is injective**, so the Abel values agree exactly when the `relPic` classes
32	   agree at every affine piece.  `abelDiv` is, componentwise, `PicEtAff.unit` of `relPicMk` of
33	   the piece's class (`abelDiv_val`), and `PicEtAff.unit_injective`
34	   (`Picard/CechKernelLemma.lean:361`, Kleiman 2.5(1) — the unconditional close of the ζ3
35	   campaign) is injective on **every** affine test algebra.  So the composite is injective iff
36	   `relPicMk ∘ picClass` is, piecewise.
37	
38	Composing: `chartValue s₁ = chartValue s₂ ↔ ∀ U, relPicMk (s₁|U).picClass =
39	relPicMk (s₂|U).picClass`.  Both directions, no hypothesis beyond the standing package.
40	
41	## What this changes about the fork, in both directions
42	
43	* **The negative branch** (build a witness): the target is not "two divisors in one linear
44	  system", and not even "two families with equal `chartValue`".  It is two locally certified
45	  systems over one affine piece whose Čech classes agree **modulo `picFromBase`** and which are
46	  not `DivEq`, stated with no twist data.  **"Strictly easier than the old target" was here and
47	  is RETRACTED** (`I-1149`): at a field test `picFromBase` is trivial, so the "modulo" buys
48	  nothing exactly where the fibrewise arguments live, and the residue is if anything the
49	  *stronger* statement.  What changed is the target's **shape**, not its price.
50	* **The positive branch** (`exists_factor`): the residue is *not* "relative GAP-2 is absent
51	  from the tree".  It is the composite of two statements, of which the tree already has the
52	  harder-looking one.  `divFam_divEq_of_eps_eq_total`
53	  (`Picard/DivSchemeMonoBridgeRel.lean:417`) is a **relative** mono over an *arbitrary*
54	  commutative test ring with **no** Noetherian hypothesis and no residual seam: two certified
55	  families with equal ε-pairs are equal in `DivFam`.  What is genuinely missing is the *other*
56	  half — that a `relPic` class separates locally certified systems at one ring — which
57	  `RelPicSeparatesDivFamZar` names below.
58	
59	  **AND HERE IS THE TRAP, which the obvious reading of the previous paragraph walks into.**
60	  It is tempting to say: the missing half is "class equality ⟹ ε-window equality", a narrow
61	  bridge, and the landed mono then finishes the job.  That framing is wrong, and reading
62	  `divisorWindow` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyWindow.lean:103`) says why: the window is the
63	  *vanishing* submodule of the divisor, `H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ − d)) ⊆ H_a ⊗ R`.  It is invariant under
64	  `DivEq` (`divisorWindow_eq_of_divEq`) but it is **not** a function of the Picard class:
65	  linearly equivalent divisors have vanishing submodules of equal *dimension* sitting as
66	  *different* subspaces, which is exactly what makes a linear system positive-dimensional.
67	
68	  So the composite would prove: equal classes ⟹ equal windows ⟹ `DivEq`, over an **arbitrary**
69	  test ring and with **no** `h⁰ = 1` hypothesis at any degree.  That is strictly stronger than
70	  the field-level keystone of DAT-C GAP-2 (`Scheme.CurveDivisor.eq_of_picClass_eq_of_h0_one`,
71	  which is in `RiemannRoch/EffectiveUniqueness.lean` — **note: outside this file's import
72	  closure, verified by `#check`**, so it is cited as background and never applied here), whose
73	  `hone` binder would become redundant.
74	
75	  **RETRACTED SENTENCE, 2026-07-30 (`I-1148`), removed rather than rephrased because it asserted
76	  a proof that does not exist.**  It read: "That dichotomy is not left as prose:
77	  `h0_eq_one_of_relPicSeparates_field` below **proves** the forcing direction at a field, from
78	  the rank anchor."  No such declaration was ever written, here or anywhere.  What *is* below is
79	  `effective_and_picClass_eq_of_picClass_eq_field`, which proves something weaker and in the
80	  other direction — class equality at a field delivers GAP-2's `hD`/`hD'`/`hcl` — and says
81	  nothing about `h⁰ = 1` being *forced*.  So the dichotomy below is an argument, not a theorem,
82	  and must be read as one.
83	
84	**MEASURED, and it is why the four sites could say what they say**: `DivSchemeMonoBridgeRel`
85	is in the import closure of **no** chart file — not `Pic0ChartPair`, not
86	`Pic0ChartUnivReduce`, not `Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion`, not
87	`Pic0ChartAbelNonInjective`, not `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre`, **and not this file either**.  The
88	absence claims are true of each file's own scope and false of the project — a scope limitation
89	this file shares rather than escapes, which is why nothing here composes the mono.
90	
91	Two facts to carry with that (`I-1151`, re-measured independently over 771 modules): exactly
92	**7** modules have the mono in closure, the only direct importer being `DivRepClassifyZarSep`;
93	and two of the seven are `DivRepChartRange` and `DivRepAffPullClause` — i.e. `rep` producers.
94	So the mono and the divisor-representability layer already sit in one closure, and *that* is
95	where a class-to-window bridge would have to be built, not in a chart file.
96	
97	## Main declarations
98	
99	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartValue_eq_iff_abelDiv_eq` — step 1, the twist cancels (an `Iff`).
100	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelDiv_eq_iff_forall_relPicMk_picClass_eq` — step 2, piecewise, from
101	  plus-unit injectivity.
102	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartValue_eq_iff_forall_relPicMk_picClass_eq` — the composite: the
103	  fork's hypothesis, twist-free and unit-free.
104	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_isChartLocusFibre_of_relPicMk_picClass_eq` — the fork's negative
105	  branch restated at the sharp target.
106	* `AlgebraicGeometry.RelPicSeparatesDivFamZar` — the residue, named at ONE test algebra.  No
107	  instance of it is proved here.
108	* `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_chartValue_of_relPicSeparates` — it suffices: piecewise
109	  separation makes the chart map injective on `divFamZar` sections at every test.
110	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicMk_picClass_mapAlgHom` /
111	  `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicSeparates_of_injective_chartValue` — **the converse**, so the residue
112	  is an *equivalence* rather than a weakening: it is the fork's own injectivity obligation
113	  renamed.  The naturality brick is the only new input.
114	* `AlgebraicGeometry.effective_and_picClass_eq_of_picClass_eq_field` — why the residue is a
115	  Riemann–Roch statement rather than plumbing: at a field, class equality already delivers
116	  GAP-2's `hD`/`hD'`/`hcl`, leaving exactly its `h⁰ = 1` binder, which the rank anchor ties to
117	  the chart's own degree.
118	* `AlgebraicGeometry.degAt_chartTwist_eq_chartParam` — the chart parameter **is** the fibre
119	  degree of the twisted class, unconditionally.  So where the fork is asked is arithmetic in `n`
120	  alone: on `chartLocus` the fibre witness has `h⁰ = n − g + 1`, which is `1` at `n = g` and
121	  `≥ 2` for `n > g`.  Every `rep` producer in this tree carries an `hchi` at its own index, which
122	  `chi_moduleKSheaf` turns into `n = genus C` (see that theorem's docstring — the pinning rests on
123	  the producers, NOT on `chi_moduleKSheaf` alone, which only converts the hypothesis and cannot
124	  supply it).  So the `n > g` case — where a refuting witness would live — cannot arise for a
125	  chart built on such a producer.  **That closes no branch**: an unrefutable hypothesis is not a
126	  satisfied one, and the datum still has no producer.
127	-/
